correctness.rationale: For each positive reference the local normalized f-exponential curve exists by f-second derivative positive at one. Its derivative is the centered weighted statistic divided by f-second derivative. Differentiating D_f in the second argument yields the exact h(u)=f(u)-u f-prime(u) equation. An explicit two-parameter equal-mean perturbation gives (h(x)-h(y))/(x-y)=h-prime(x) for every x>1 and 0<y<1. Differentiation in y forces h-prime constant, and integration yields precisely positive KL multiples plus affine generator. The KL converse is globally convex in the exponential parameter; binary minimality follows from normalization plus the sole moment. Code checks 175 rational KL identities, 49 parameter realizations and a Pearson exact counterexample. Finite tests are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The directly motivating 2026 theorem assumes entropy adaptedness over every finite support; its Remark 18 uses five points in the single-statistic case and its ternary figures only show two particular failures. This theorem derives rigidity from a fixed three-point support and local stationarity only. The 2014 Bregman/sufficiency characterization has genuinely different, stronger full-divergence premises and does not imply the local witness. Actual mathematical-search queries and prior research-claim comparisons did not identify a covering fixed-ternary criterion; implicit prior equivalence remains a risk.

value.rationale: The characterization pinpoints the minimal nonvacuous alphabet for detecting KL information-projection rigidity with a single first moment. It strengthens a recently motivated five-point/all-support proof framework to one fixed ternary configuration and to an infinitesimal stationarity test. Exact size minimality and the structural all-generators condition make this a motivated mathematical boundary, not an arbitrary computed slice. It does not claim a generalization to degenerate curvature or higher-moment families.
